description: The plot illustrates how the metric labeled “Loss” changes over “Training Time (s)” for two methods, “Vanilla” and “SepLLM.” The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)” on a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 250,000 seconds with major tick labels at 0, 50,000, 100,000, 150,000, 200,000, and 250,000. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75 with tick labels at 0.05 increments (2.40, 2.45, …, 2.75). The “Vanilla” series is drawn as a purple solid line with triangle markers; it starts near the top of the axis around 2.75 at very small training times, then decreases smoothly, reaching about 2.60 around 50,000 s, about 2.56 around 100,000 s, about 2.54 around 150,000 s, and ending near 2.50 at 250,000 s. The “SepLLM” series is drawn as a red solid line with circular markers; it also begins near 2.75 at very small training times and declines smoothly, reaching roughly 2.60 around 50,000 s, about 2.56 around 100,000 s, about 2.53 around 150,000 s, and ending slightly below 2.50 (around 2.49) near 250,000 s. A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at Loss = 2.50, and a green dashed vertical bracketed region appears roughly between 190,000 s and 240,000 s with a green annotation reading “1.26×” above it.
